outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Landscape of Large Language Model Training
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by examining the current state of training Large Language Models (LLMs). It discusses the high demands of full 16-bit finetuning, the limitations of standard quantization methods in a training context, and the motivation behind parameter-efficient strategies like LoRA.
subtopics: The computational cost of full 16-bit finetuning on massive models (e.g., LLaMA 65B).
The history and mechanics of block-wise k-bit quantization for inference.
Why standard quantization techniques fail during backpropagation.
Introduction to Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) and Low-rank Adapters (LoRA).
The problem statement: How to train quantized models without catastrophic performance degradation.

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Foundations of QLoRA Technical Infrastructure
outline.description: This chapter delves into the specific mathematical and engineering innovations that make QLoRA possible. It provides a deep dive into the custom data types, optimization techniques, and memory management strategies used to reduce memory footprint while maintaining precision.
subtopics: 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4): Information-theoretic quantization for normal distributions.
Why NF4 outperforms integer-based 4-bit (Int4) and FP4 standards.
Double Quantization: Reducing the memory footprint of quantization constants via FP8 storage.
The interplay between storage data types (NF4) and computation data types (BFloat16).
Paged Optimizers: Leveraging NVIDIA unified memory to handle gradient checkpointing spikes.
Formal mathematical formulation of QLoRA forward and backward passes.

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Validating Performance with Precision Recovery
outline.description: This chapter presents empirical evidence proving that QLoRA can recover the full performance capabilities of a model by adapting a quantized base model to match fully finetuned baselines. It focuses on controlled experiments across different model sizes and architectures.
subtopics: Experimental setup: Comparing NF4-QLoRA against Full-Finetune (16-bit) and standard LoRA.
Case study: RoBERTa and T5 models; achieving parity with full finetuning on small scales.
Scaling up: Analyzing performance on LLaMA models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters.
'The Adapter Layer' phenomenon: Why applying LoRA to all transformer layers is critical for high-fidelity tuning.
#breakthrough# Evidence that 4-bit accuracy is not permanent loss but recoverable information deficit.
#breakthrough# Benchmarking against alternative baselines: Does FP4 lose more than NF4?
